items.stem: In a hypothesis test, the null hypothesis is
options: the hypothesis assumed to be true unless there is sufficient evidence against it
always a statement that a parameter has changed
the hypothesis that the sample result is correct
the hypothesis the researcher wants to prove
items.answer: the hypothesis assumed to be true unless there is sufficient evidence against it
items.markingKey: H₀ is assumed true; the test looks for evidence against it. [1]

items.stem: Explain why hypotheses are stated in terms of a population parameter and not the sample result.
items.answer: The sample result is known; the test is about the unknown population value (p, λ or μ) from which the sample came, and whether the sample is consistent with the value in H₀.
items.markingKey: B1 sample value known; B1 inference about population parameter [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a one-tailed and a two-tailed test.
items.answer: A one-tailed test looks for a change in one specified direction (H₁ uses < or >); a two-tailed test looks for a change in either direction (H₁ uses ≠) and splits the significance level between both tails.
items.markingKey: B1 one direction vs either; B1 significance level split between tails [2]

items.stem: A seed company states that 75% of its tomato seeds germinate. A gardener in Accra wishes to test whether the germination rate is higher than stated. The gardener plants 15 randomly chosen seeds and 15 of them germinate. State suitable hypotheses for a test at the 2.5% significance level and, given that P(X ≥ 15) = 0.0134, state the conclusion.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.75, H₁: p > 0.75. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the germination rate is higher than stated.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.75, H₁: p > 0.75; M1 compare with 0.025; A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: In the past, 15% of the buses on a route in Auckland arrived late. After a new timetable is introduced, the bus company tests whether the proportion of late buses has changed. Of 12 randomly chosen buses after the change, 4 arrived late. Given that P(X ≥ 4) = 0.0922, state suitable hypotheses and carry out the test at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.15, H₁: p ≠ 0.15. Two-tailed: 0.0922 > 0.005. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the proportion of late buses has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.15, H₁: p ≠ 0.15; M1 compare with 0.005 (half of 1%); A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: In the past, 30% of the customers at a café in Toronto ordered a cold drink. After the menu is changed, the owner wishes to test whether this proportion has changed. In a random sample of 10 customers after the change, 7 ordered a cold drink. (a) Explain why a two-tailed test is appropriate. (b) Explain what is meant by the significance level in this context. (c) State one assumption needed for the binomial model to be valid.
items.answer: (a) A change in either direction is of interest (the proportion of customers who order a cold drink has changed). (b) The probability, 0.05, of concluding that the proportion of customers who order a cold drink has changed when in fact p = 0.3. (c) The customers are independent of each other (with the same probability of success for each).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 probability of rejecting H₀ when true; B1 in context [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: The significance level of a test is
options: the probability that H₁ is true
the probability of rejecting H₀ when H₀ is true
the probability that H₀ is true
the probability of accepting H₀ when it is false
items.answer: the probability of rejecting H₀ when H₀ is true
items.markingKey: Significance level = P(reject H₀ | H₀ true). [1]

items.stem: Explain why "do not reject H₀" is preferred to "accept H₀" as a conclusion.
items.answer: Failing to find evidence against H₀ does not show that H₀ is true; the sample is simply consistent with H₀.
items.markingKey: B1 lack of evidence; B1 not proof that H₀ is true [2]

items.stem: Explain why a researcher should choose the hypotheses and significance level before collecting the data.
items.answer: Choosing them after seeing the data could bias the test, e.g. choosing a tail or level that makes the result significant.
items.markingKey: B1 avoids bias; B1 example of choosing tail or level to suit the data [2]

items.stem: Tomás is an archer who hits the centre of the target with probability 0.3. After a new coaching programme, Tomás wishes to test whether this probability has decreased. In 20 shots after the programme, Tomás hits the centre 4 times. A test is carried out at the 10% significance level. Hana finds that the result is not significant and concludes: "This proves that H₀ is true.". Explain the mistake.
items.answer: Not rejecting H₀ only means there is insufficient evidence against it; it does not prove that H₀ is true. The conclusion should be "there is insufficient evidence that Tomás's probability of hitting the centre has decreased".
items.markingKey: B1 no proof that H₀ is true; B1 correct form of conclusion [2]

items.stem: Mohammed suspects that a coin is biased towards heads. The coin is tossed 12 times and shows heads 11 times. State suitable hypotheses for a test at the 1% significance level and, given that P(X ≥ 11) = 0.00317, state the conclusion.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p > 0.5. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the coin is biased towards heads.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p > 0.5; M1 compare with 0.01; A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: Ethan suspects that a coin is biased towards heads. The coin is tossed 18 times and shows heads 12 times. State suitable hypotheses for a test at the 5% significance level and, given that P(X ≥ 12) = 0.119, state the conclusion.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p > 0.5. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the coin is biased towards heads.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p > 0.5; M1 compare with 0.05; A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: Grace is an archer who hits the centre of the target with probability 0.4. After a new coaching programme, Grace wishes to test whether this probability has changed. In 24 shots after the programme, Grace hits the centre 17 times. Given that P(X ≥ 17) = 0.00220, state suitable hypotheses and carry out the test at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p ≠ 0.4. Two-tailed: 0.00220 < 0.005. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that Grace's probability of hitting the centre has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p ≠ 0.4; M1 compare with 0.005 (half of 1%); A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: A seed company states that 70% of its tomato seeds germinate. A gardener in Accra wishes to test whether the germination rate is lower than stated. The gardener plants 12 randomly chosen seeds and 6 of them germinate. (a) Explain why a one-tailed test is appropriate. (b) Explain what is meant by the significance level in this context. (c) State one assumption needed for the binomial model to be valid.
items.answer: (a) The suspicion is only that the germination rate is lower than stated, in one direction. (b) The probability, 0.05, of concluding that the germination rate is lower than stated when in fact p = 0.7. (c) The seeds are independent of each other (with the same probability of success for each).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 probability of rejecting H₀ when true; B1 in context [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: Lucas suspects that a coin is biased. The coin is tossed 18 times and shows heads 12 times. (a) Explain why a two-tailed test is appropriate. (b) Carry out the test at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: (a) A change in either direction is of interest (the coin is biased). (b) H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p ≠ 0.5; P(X ≥ 12) = 0.119 > 0.005. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the coin is biased.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p ≠ 0.5; M1 P(X ≥ 12) with X ~ B(18, 0.5) = 1 − P(X ≤ 11); A1 0.119; M1 compare with 0.005 (two-tailed, so half of the significance level); A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: In a test of H₀: p = 0.3 against H₁: p > 0.3 with X ~ B(20, 0.3), 10 successes are observed. The probability compared with the significance level is
items.markingKey: Values at least as extreme as the observed value. [1]

items.stem: Explain why, for a binomial test, the probability of the observed value or a more extreme value is used rather than the probability of the observed value alone.
items.answer: Any single value can have a small probability; the test asks how likely a result at least as extreme as the observed one is when H₀ is true.
items.markingKey: B1 single values have small probabilities; B1 tail probability measures extremeness [2]

items.stem: Explain why the actual significance level of a test based on the Poisson distribution is often not exactly 5%.
items.answer: The distribution is discrete, so the tail probabilities jump in steps and there is usually no critical region with probability exactly 0.05.
items.markingKey: B1 discrete; B1 probabilities in steps [2]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Ana does better than guessing at random. Ana answers 20 questions and gets 10 correct. Test at the 2.5% significance level whether Ana does better than guessing at random.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.25, H₁: p > 0.25; P(X ≥ 10) = 0.0139 < 0.025. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that Ana does better than guessing at random.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.25, H₁: p > 0.25; M1 P(X ≥ 10) with X ~ B(20, 0.25) = 1 − P(X ≤ 9); A1 0.0139; M1 compare with 0.025; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The number of bacteria in 1 ml of river water taken near a factory in Cape Town has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.6. After the factory closes, a scientist wishes to test whether the mean number of bacteria has decreased. In a randomly chosen 4 ml sample, the number of bacteria is 1. Carry out the test at the 5% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: λ = 1.6, H₁: λ < 1.6; X ~ Po(6.4); P(X ≤ 1) = 0.0123 < 0.05. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean number of bacteria has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: λ = 1.6, H₁: λ < 1.6 (or in terms of the mean for a 4 ml sample); B1 mean for a 4 ml sample = 6.4; M1 P(X ≤ 1) with X ~ Po(6.4); A1 0.0123; M1 compare with 0.05; A1 conclusion in context [6]

items.stem: The number of bacteria in 1 ml of river water taken near a factory in Accra has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.4. After the factory closes, a scientist wishes to test whether the mean number of bacteria has changed. In a randomly chosen 2 ml sample, the number of bacteria is 13. Carry out the test at the 10% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: λ = 2.4, H₁: λ ≠ 2.4; X ~ Po(4.8); P(X ≥ 13) = 0.00142 < 0.05. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean number of bacteria has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: λ = 2.4, H₁: λ ≠ 2.4 (or in terms of the mean for a 2 ml sample); B1 mean for a 2 ml sample = 4.8; M1 P(X ≥ 13) with X ~ Po(4.8) = 1 − P(X ≤ 12); A1 0.00142; M1 compare with 0.05; A1 conclusion in context [6]

items.stem: The number of bacteria in 1 ml of river water taken near a factory in Lima has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.4. After the factory closes, a scientist wishes to test whether the mean number of bacteria has decreased. The test uses the number in a randomly chosen 5 ml sample and a 10% significance level. (a) State the null and alternative hypotheses. (b) Find the critical region.

A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Diego does better than guessing at random. The test uses 15 questions and a 5% significance level. (a) Find the critical region. (b) The observed value is 7. State the conclusion of the test.
items.answer: (a) X ≥ 8 (b) Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that Diego does better than guessing at random.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 P(X ≥ 8) = 0.0173 ≤ 0.05; M1 P(X ≥ 7) = 0.0566 > 0.05; A1 X ≥ 8 [3] (b) M1 7 not in critical region; A1 conclusion in context [2]

items.stem: In a test of H₀: λ = 4 against H₁: λ < 4 with X ~ Po(4), 1 event is observed. The probability compared with the significance level is
The mean number of events in 1 hour is 2.5. Under H₀, the distribution of the number of events in 4 hours is

A factory in Kathmandu has found that 20% of the components it makes are faulty. After new machinery is installed, the manager tests whether the proportion of faulty components has increased. In a random sample of 12 components made by the new machinery, the number of faulty components is 6. The hypotheses are H₀: p = 0.2, H₁: p > 0.2. Find the probability that is compared with the significance level.

The number of earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more in a region in a year has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.2. A geologist wishes to test whether the mean number of such earthquakes has increased. In a randomly chosen 5-year period, the number of such earthquakes is 8. The test is at the 2.5% significance level. Diego calculates P(X = 8) = 0.103 using Po(6) and compares it with 0.025. Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: A tail probability is needed: P(X ≥ 8) = 0.256. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean number of earthquakes has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 tail probability needed; M1 0.256; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The number of customers arriving at a shop in Seoul in a 5-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 2. After an advertising campaign, the owner wishes to test whether the mean number of customers arriving has increased. In a randomly chosen 10-minute period, the number of customers arriving is 6. The test is at the 10% significance level. Samuel calculates P(X > 6) = 0.111 using Po(4). Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The observed value must be included: P(X ≥ 6) = 0.215. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean number of customers arriving has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 observed value 6 must be included; M1 0.215; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The number of bacteria in 1 ml of river water taken near a factory in Hanoi has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.6. After the factory closes, a scientist wishes to test whether the mean number of bacteria has increased. In a randomly chosen 2 ml sample, the number of bacteria is 9. The test is at the 1% significance level. Mohammed calculates P(X = 9) = 0.00395 using Po(3.2) and compares it with 0.01. Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: A tail probability is needed: P(X ≥ 9) = 0.00571. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean number of bacteria has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 tail probability needed; M1 0.00571; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: A national survey found that 40% of adults in Dhaka read a daily newspaper. A journalist wishes to test whether the proportion for young adults is lower. In a random sample of 8 young adults, 2 read a daily newspaper. Test at the 10% significance level whether the proportion for young adults is lower.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p < 0.4; P(X ≤ 2) = 0.315 > 0.1. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the proportion for young adults is lower.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p < 0.4; M1 P(X ≤ 2) with X ~ B(8, 0.4); A1 0.315; M1 compare with 0.1; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: Tariq is an archer who hits the centre of the target with probability 0.4. After a new coaching programme, Tariq wishes to test whether this probability has decreased. In 16 shots after the programme, Tariq hits the centre 4 times. Test at the 10% significance level whether Tariq's probability of hitting the centre has decreased.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p < 0.4; P(X ≤ 4) = 0.167 > 0.1. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that Tariq's probability of hitting the centre has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.4, H₁: p < 0.4; M1 P(X ≤ 4) with X ~ B(16, 0.4); A1 0.167; M1 compare with 0.1; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Grace does better than guessing at random. The test is to be based on 18 questions. Using a 5% significance level, find the critical region.

A national survey found that 30% of adults in Toronto read a daily newspaper. A journalist wishes to test whether the proportion for young adults is higher. A random sample of 10 young adults is to be used for the test. Using a 2.5% significance level, find the critical region.

A national survey found that 45% of adults in Istanbul read a daily newspaper. A journalist wishes to test whether the proportion for young adults is higher. The test uses 12 young adults and a 5% significance level. (a) Find the critical region. (b) State the probability of a Type I error.

In the past, 30% of the buses on a route in Hanoi arrived late. After a new timetable is introduced, the bus company tests whether the proportion of late buses has decreased. The test uses 20 buses and a 2.5% significance level. (a) State the null and alternative hypotheses. (b) Find the critical region. (c) State the probability of a Type I error.
In a test for a population mean with known σ, the test statistic is
options: z = (x̄ − μ₀)/(σ²/n)
z = (x̄ − μ₀)/(σ/n)
z = (x̄ − μ₀)/σ
items.markingKey: The sample mean has standard deviation σ/√n. [1]

items.stem: Explain why a test for a population mean can be carried out using a large sample even when the population is not normally distributed.
items.answer: By the central limit theorem the sample mean is approximately normally distributed when n is large, whatever the population distribution.
items.markingKey: B1 CLT; B1 applies to the sample mean for large n [2]

items.stem: Explain why, when σ is unknown and the sample is large, the unbiased estimate s² can be used in place of σ².
items.answer: For a large sample s² is a reliable estimate of σ², so (x̄ − μ)/(s/√n) is approximately N(0, 1).
items.markingKey: B1 large sample so s² close to σ²; B1 test statistic approximately standard normal [2]

items.stem: The heights of sunflowers of a certain variety grown in Kathmandu are normally distributed with mean 180 cm and standard deviation 18 cm. A farmer uses a new fertiliser and wishes to test whether the mean height has decreased. A random sample of 20 sunflowers grown with the fertiliser has mean height 175.5 cm. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 2.5% significance level whether the mean height has decreased.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 180, H₁: μ < 180; z = −1.118 > −1.96. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean height has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 180, H₁: μ < 180; M1 z = (175.5 − 180)/(18/√20); A1 −1.118; M1 compare with −1.96; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The masses of bags of rice filled by a machine are normally distributed with mean 750 g and standard deviation 5 g. After the machine is serviced, the manager wishes to test whether the mean mass has changed. A random sample of 25 bags filled after the service has mean mass 746.9 g. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean mass has changed.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 750, H₁: μ ≠ 750; z = −3.100 < −1.96. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean mass has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 750, H₁: μ ≠ 750; M1 z = (746.9 − 750)/(5/√25); A1 −3.100; M1 compare with −1.96 (two-tailed); A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: In the past, the masses of bags of rice filled by a machine had mean 500 g. After the machine is serviced, the manager wishes to test whether the mean mass has increased. For a random sample of 40 bags, the values x g satisfy Σx = 20020 and Σx² = 10020664.4. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean mass has increased.
items.answer: x̄ = 500.5, s² = 16.78; H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ > 500; z = 0.772; compare with 2.326. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean mass has increased.

items.stem: In the past, the heights of sunflowers of a certain variety grown in Manila had mean 150 cm. A farmer uses a new fertiliser and wishes to test whether the mean height has decreased. For a random sample of 50 sunflowers, the values x cm satisfy Σx = 7380 and Σx² = 1112164.8. (a) Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean height has decreased. (b) Explain why it is not necessary to know that the population is normally distributed.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 150, H₁: μ < 150; z = −0.785; Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean height has decreased. (b) n = 50 is large, so by the central limit theorem x̄ is approximately normal.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 150, H₁: μ < 150; M1 z = (147.6 − 150)/√(466.9/50); A1 −0.785; M1 compare with −1.282; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) B1 large n; B1 CLT [2]

items.stem: In the past, the volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine had mean 330 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is less than this. For a random sample of 120 cartons, the values x ml satisfy Σx = 39540 and Σx² = 13037922.1. (a) Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean volume is less than this. (b) State, with a reason, whether the conclusion would be the same at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 330, H₁: μ < 330; z = −0.613; Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean volume is less than this. (b) Critical value −2.326; z = −0.613, so do not reject H₀; the same conclusion.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 330, H₁: μ < 330; M1 z = (329.5 − 330)/√(79.77/120); A1 −0.613; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) M1 compare with 2.326; A1 correct comparison [2]

items.stem: A one-tailed test of H₀: μ = 50 against H₁: μ > 50 at the 5% level rejects H₀ if

The reaction times of drivers in a simulator test have mean 220 ms and standard deviation 30 ms. A researcher wishes to test whether the mean reaction time of drivers who have just used a phone is lower. A random sample of 100 drivers who have just used a phone has mean reaction time 215.1 ms. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 2.5% significance level. Tariq calculates z = (215.1 − 220)/(30²/100) = −0.544. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The variance σ²/n has been used instead of the standard deviation σ/√n; z = −1.633. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower.
items.markingKey: B1 square root of σ²/n needed; M1 z = −1.633; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The times taken by employees in Bangkok to complete a task have mean 24 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes. After a training session, the manager wishes to test whether the mean time has increased. 64 randomly chosen employees who attended the training have a mean time of 26 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 1% significance level. Isla calculates z = (26 − 24)/(5²/64) = 5.120. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The variance σ²/n has been used instead of the standard deviation σ/√n; z = 3.200. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean time has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 square root of σ²/n needed; M1 z = 3.200; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The journey times on a bus route in Bogotá have mean 55 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. After a new bus lane opens, the bus company wishes to test whether the mean journey time has changed. 40 randomly chosen journeys after the bus lane opens have a mean time of 56.1 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 10% significance level. Chloe calculates z = (56.1 − 55)/6 = 0.183. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The standard deviation of the sample mean is σ/√n, so z = (56.1 − 55)/(6/√40) = 1.160. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean journey time has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 should divide by σ/√n; M1 z = 1.160; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The masses of apples from an orchard have mean 150 g and standard deviation 15 g. After a change of irrigation method, the owner wishes to test whether the mean mass has decreased. A random sample of 36 apples picked after the change has mean mass 144.7 g. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 10% significance level. Felix calculates z = (144.7 − 150)/(15²/36) = −0.848. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The variance σ²/n has been used instead of the standard deviation σ/√n; z = −2.120. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean mass of the apples has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 square root of σ²/n needed; M1 z = −2.120; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The times taken by employees in Nairobi to complete a task have mean 45 minutes and standard deviation 4 minutes. After a training session, the manager wishes to test whether the mean time has decreased. 64 randomly chosen employees who attended the training have a mean time of 43.9 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 10% significance level. Ravi calculates z = (43.9 − 45)/4 = −0.275. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The standard deviation of the sample mean is σ/√n, so z = (43.9 − 45)/(4/√64) = −2.200. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean time has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 should divide by σ/√n; M1 z = −2.200; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The reaction times of drivers in a simulator test have mean 250 ms and standard deviation 30 ms. A researcher wishes to test whether the mean reaction time of drivers who have just used a phone is lower. A random sample of 40 drivers who have just used a phone has mean reaction time 239.8 ms. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 250, H₁: μ < 250; z = −2.150 < −1.645. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 250, H₁: μ < 250; M1 z = (239.8 − 250)/(30/√40); A1 −2.150; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine are normally distributed with mean 1000 ml and standard deviation 3 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is less than this. A random sample of 16 cartons has mean volume 998.6 ml. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean volume is less than this.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 1000, H₁: μ < 1000; z = −1.867 < −1.282. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean volume is less than this.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 1000, H₁: μ < 1000; M1 z = (998.6 − 1000)/(3/√16); A1 −1.867; M1 compare with −1.282; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The reaction times of drivers in a simulator test have mean 280 ms and standard deviation 40 ms. A researcher wishes to test whether the mean reaction time of drivers who have just used a phone is different. A random sample of 100 drivers who have just used a phone has mean reaction time 292.8 ms. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean reaction time of such drivers is different.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 280, H₁: μ ≠ 280; z = 3.200 > 2.576. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean reaction time of such drivers is different.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 280, H₁: μ ≠ 280; M1 z = (292.8 − 280)/(40/√100); A1 3.200; M1 compare with 2.576 (two-tailed); A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: In the past, the journey times on a bus route in Hanoi had mean 55 minutes. After a new bus lane opens, the bus company wishes to test whether the mean journey time has decreased. For a random sample of 100 journeys, the values x minutes satisfy Σx = 5450 and Σx² = 300189.2. (a) Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean journey time has decreased. (b) Explain why it is not necessary to know that the population is normally distributed.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 55, H₁: μ < 55; z = −0.884; Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean journey time has decreased. (b) n = 100 is large, so by the central limit theorem x̄ is approximately normal.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 55, H₁: μ < 55; M1 z = (54.5 − 55)/√(31.96/100); A1 −0.884; M1 compare with −1.282; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) B1 large n; B1 CLT [2]

items.stem: In the past, the reaction times of drivers in a simulator test had mean 220 ms. A researcher wishes to test whether the mean reaction time of drivers who have just used a phone is lower. For a random sample of 60 drivers, the values x ms satisfy Σx = 13038 and Σx² = 2879284.2. (a) Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower. (b) State, with a reason, whether the conclusion would be the same at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 220, H₁: μ < 220; z = −0.748; Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower. (b) Critical value −2.326; z = −0.748, so do not reject H₀; the same conclusion.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 220, H₁: μ < 220; M1 z = (217.3 − 220)/√(781.8/60); A1 −0.748; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) M1 compare with 2.326; A1 correct comparison [2]

items.stem: In the past, the lifetimes of batteries of a certain brand had mean 240 hours. A consumer group wishes to test whether the mean lifetime is more than this. For a random sample of 80 batteries, the values x hours satisfy Σx = 19960 and Σx² = 5051353.4. (a) Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean lifetime is more than this. (b) State, with a reason, whether the conclusion would be the same at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 240, H₁: μ > 240; z = 2.828; Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean lifetime is more than this. (b) Critical value 2.326; z = 2.828, so reject H₀; the same conclusion.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 240, H₁: μ > 240; M1 z = (249.5 − 240)/√(903.0/80); A1 2.828; M1 compare with 1.645; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) M1 compare with 2.326; A1 correct comparison [2]

items.stem: A Type I error occurs when
options: H₀ is rejected when it is true
H₁ is rejected when it is true
H₀ is not rejected when it is false
the test statistic is calculated incorrectly
items.answer: H₀ is rejected when it is true

items.stem: Explain why the probability of a Type II error can only be calculated if a particular value of the parameter is given.
items.answer: A Type II error occurs when H₀ is false; its probability depends on the actual (true) value of the parameter, which H₁ does not specify.
items.markingKey: B1 H₁ gives a range of values; B1 probability depends on the true value [2]

items.stem: Explain how the probability of a Type II error can be reduced without increasing the probability of a Type I error.
items.answer: Increase the sample size: the sampling distribution becomes narrower, so the test is more likely to detect a real change.
items.markingKey: B1 larger sample; B1 reason [2]

items.stem: A seed company states that 70% of its tomato seeds germinate. A gardener in Cape Town wishes to test whether the germination rate is lower than stated. The test is based on 10 seeds, and H₀ is rejected if X ≤ 3, where X is the number of successes. Find the probability of a Type I error.

The number of meteors seen by an observer in Lisbon in a 10-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.5. An astronomer moves to a new observing site and wishes to test whether the mean number of meteors seen has decreased. The test uses the number, X, in a randomly chosen one-hour period; H₀ is rejected if X ≤ 2. Find the probability of a Type I error, and the probability of a Type II error if in fact the mean for a 10-minute period is 0.6.
items.answer: P(Type I) = 0.00623; P(Type II) = 0.697

items.stem: The masses of apples from an orchard are normally distributed with mean 150 g and standard deviation 12 g. After a change of irrigation method, the owner wishes to test whether the mean mass has increased. A random sample of 40 apples is to be used to test H₀: μ = 150, H₁: μ > 150 at the 5% significance level. (a) Find the set of values of the sample mean for which H₀ is rejected. (b) State the effect on the probability of a Type II error of using a larger sample, with the same significance level.
items.answer: (a) x̄ > 153.1 (b) It decreases, because σ/√n is smaller so the distributions of x̄ under the two values of μ overlap less.

items.stem: A Type II error occurs when
options: H₀ is rejected when it is false
the significance level is too small
H₀ is not rejected when it is false
H₀ is rejected when it is true
items.answer: H₀ is not rejected when it is false

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Reducing the significance level of a test (with the same sample size) will usually (b) A Type I error occurs when
items.answer: (a) increase the probability of a Type II error (b) H₀ is rejected when it is true
items.markingKey: (a) A smaller critical region makes failing to reject a false H₀ more likely. [1] (b) [1]

items.stem: In the past, 15% of the buses on a route in Bangkok arrived late. After a new timetable is introduced, the bus company tests whether the proportion of late buses has increased. The test uses 18 buses at the 1% significance level, and H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 8. Mei says: "A Type I error is concluding that the proportion of late buses has increased when it really has." Explain why Mei is wrong.
items.answer: That is a correct decision. A Type I error is rejecting H₀ when it is true: concluding that the proportion of late buses has increased when in fact p = 0.15.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the error; B1 correct description in context [2]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Ana does better than guessing at random. The test uses 16 questions at the 10% significance level, and H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 7. Diego says: "P(Type I error) = 0.0796, so P(Type II error) = 1 − 0.0796 = 0.920." Explain why Diego is wrong.
items.answer: Type I and Type II errors are not complementary: a Type II error is not rejecting H₀ when it is false, and its probability depends on the true value of p, which is not given.
items.markingKey: B1 not complementary; B1 depends on the true value of p [2]

items.stem: The volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine have mean 250 ml and standard deviation 3 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is different from this. A random sample of 30 cartons is used to test H₀: μ = 250, H₁: μ ≠ 250 at the 1% significance level. State the probability of a Type I error.
items.markingKey: For a continuous test statistic, P(Type I error) = significance level. [1]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Tariq does better than guessing at random. The test is based on 20 questions, and H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 9, where X is the number of successes. Find the probability of a Type I error.

The number of bacteria in 1 ml of river water taken near a factory in Bogotá has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.6. After the factory closes, a scientist wishes to test whether the mean number of bacteria has increased. The test uses the number, X, in a randomly chosen 5 ml sample; H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 15. Find the probability of a Type I error.

The number of flaws in a 1-metre length of fabric from a mill has a Poisson distribution with mean 0.6. After a new loom is installed, the manager wishes to test whether the mean number of flaws has increased. The test uses the number, X, in a randomly chosen 10-metre length; H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 11. Find the probability of a Type I error, and the probability of a Type II error if in fact the mean for a 1-metre length of fabric from a mill is 1.2.
items.answer: P(Type I) = 0.0426; P(Type II) = 0.347

items.stem: Yusuf is an archer who hits the centre of the target with probability 0.2. After a new coaching programme, Yusuf wishes to test whether this probability has increased. The test is based on 18 shots and uses a 2.5% significance level. (a) State suitable hypotheses and find the critical region. (b) Find the probability of a Type I error.
A test of H₀: p = 0.4 against H₁: p ≠ 0.4 is
options: a two-tailed test
a one-tailed test
a test about the sample proportion
a test with no critical region
items.answer: a two-tailed test
items.markingKey: H₁ allows values on both sides of 0.4. [1]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Grace does better than guessing at random. Grace answers 10 questions and gets 5 correct. A test is carried out at the 5% significance level. Mei writes H₁: p < 0.25. Explain the mistake.
items.answer: H₁ must match the suspicion that Grace does better than guessing at random, so H₁: p > 0.25.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies wrong direction; B1 correct alternative hypothesis [2]

items.stem: Samuel is an archer who hits the centre of the target with probability 0.3. After a new coaching programme, Samuel wishes to test whether this probability has decreased. In 20 shots after the programme, Samuel hits the centre 0 times. State suitable hypotheses for a test at the 10% significance level and, given that P(X ≤ 0) = 0.000798, state the conclusion.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.3, H₁: p < 0.3. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that Samuel's probability of hitting the centre has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.3, H₁: p < 0.3; M1 compare with 0.1; A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: A national survey found that 35% of adults in Lagos read a daily newspaper. A journalist wishes to test whether the proportion for young adults is lower. In a random sample of 18 young adults, 2 read a daily newspaper. (a) Explain why a one-tailed test is appropriate. (b) Explain what is meant by the significance level in this context. (c) State one assumption needed for the binomial model to be valid.
items.answer: (a) The suspicion is only that the proportion for young adults is lower, in one direction. (b) The probability, 0.05, of concluding that the proportion for young adults is lower when in fact p = 0.35. (c) The young adults are independent of each other (with the same probability of success for each).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 probability of rejecting H₀ when true; B1 in context [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: For a discrete test statistic the actual significance level of a test is usually
options: exactly equal to the stated level
equal to 0.5
less than the stated significance level
greater than the stated level
items.answer: less than the stated significance level
items.markingKey: The critical region is chosen so its probability does not exceed the stated level. [1]

items.stem: The number of flaws in a 1-metre length of fabric from a mill has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.5. After a new loom is installed, the manager wishes to test whether the mean number of flaws has decreased. In a randomly chosen 10-metre length, the number of flaws is 10. The test is at the 10% significance level. Sofia calculates P(X < 10) = 0.0699 using Po(15). Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The observed value must be included: P(X ≤ 10) = 0.118. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean number of flaws has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 observed value 10 must be included; M1 0.118; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The number of typing errors made by a typist in a page has a Poisson distribution with mean 0.6. After a training course, the typist wishes to test whether the mean number of errors has decreased. In a randomly chosen 5-page report, the number of errors is 1. The test is at the 5% significance level. Arjun uses X ~ Po(0.6) and finds P(X ≤ 1) = 0.878. Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The mean must be scaled to a 5-page report: X ~ Po(3), giving P(X ≤ 1) = 0.199. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean number of errors has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 mean should be 3; M1 0.199; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: In the past, 25% of the customers at a café in Mumbai ordered a cold drink. After the menu is changed, the owner wishes to test whether this proportion has decreased. In a random sample of 18 customers after the change, 0 ordered a cold drink. Test at the 2.5% significance level whether the proportion of customers who order a cold drink has decreased.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.25, H₁: p < 0.25; P(X ≤ 0) = 0.00564 < 0.025. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the proportion of customers who order a cold drink has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.25, H₁: p < 0.25; M1 P(X ≤ 0) with X ~ B(18, 0.25); A1 0.00564; M1 compare with 0.025; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The number of emails received by an office manager in an hour has a Poisson distribution with mean 3.6. After a new spam filter is installed, the manager wishes to test whether the mean number of emails has decreased. In a randomly chosen 3-hour period, the number of emails received is 3. Carry out the test at the 2.5% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: λ = 3.6, H₁: λ < 3.6; X ~ Po(10.8); P(X ≤ 3) = 0.00571 < 0.025. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean number of emails has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: λ = 3.6, H₁: λ < 3.6 (or in terms of the mean for a 3-hour period); B1 mean for a 3-hour period = 10.8; M1 P(X ≤ 3) with X ~ Po(10.8); A1 0.00571; M1 compare with 0.025; A1 conclusion in context [6]

items.stem: A seed company states that 85% of its tomato seeds germinate. A gardener in Kuala Lumpur wishes to test whether the germination rate is higher than stated. The test uses 25 seeds and a 5% significance level. (a) State the null and alternative hypotheses. (b) Find the critical region. (c) State the probability of a Type I error.

The masses of bags of rice filled by a machine have mean 750 g and standard deviation 6 g. After the machine is serviced, the manager wishes to test whether the mean mass has decreased. A random sample of 50 bags filled after the service has mean mass 748.8 g. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Find the value of the test statistic z.

The journey times on a bus route in Hanoi have mean 55 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. After a new bus lane opens, the bus company wishes to test whether the mean journey time has changed. 30 randomly chosen journeys after the bus lane opens have a mean time of 52.7 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 1% significance level. Ethan calculates z = (52.7 − 55)/6 = −0.383. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The standard deviation of the sample mean is σ/√n, so z = (52.7 − 55)/(6/√30) = −2.100. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean journey time has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 should divide by σ/√n; M1 z = −2.100; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The masses of bags of rice filled by a machine are normally distributed with mean 500 g and standard deviation 4 g. After the machine is serviced, the manager wishes to test whether the mean mass has decreased. A random sample of 20 bags filled after the service has mean mass 497.3 g. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 2.5% significance level whether the mean mass has decreased.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ < 500; z = −3.019 < −1.96. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean mass has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ < 500; M1 z = (497.3 − 500)/(4/√20); A1 −3.019; M1 compare with −1.96; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The masses of apples from an orchard have mean 120 g and standard deviation 12 g. After a change of irrigation method, the owner wishes to test whether the mean mass has increased. Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean mass of the apples has increased.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 120, H₁: μ > 120; z = 1.871 > 1.282. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean mass of the apples has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 120, H₁: μ > 120; M1 z = (124.1 − 120)/(12/√30); A1 1.871; M1 compare with 1.282; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The heights of sunflowers of a certain variety grown in Lisbon have mean 200 cm and standard deviation 20 cm. A farmer uses a new fertiliser and wishes to test whether the mean height has changed. A random sample of 30 sunflowers grown with the fertiliser has mean height 188.2 cm. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean height has changed.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 200, H₁: μ ≠ 200; z = −3.232 < −2.576. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean height has changed.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 200, H₁: μ ≠ 200; M1 z = (188.2 − 200)/(20/√30); A1 −3.232; M1 compare with −2.576 (two-tailed); A1 conclusion in context [5]

(b) Explain why it is not necessary to know that the population is normally distributed.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 150, H₁: μ > 150; z = 0.460; Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean height has increased. (b) n = 50 is large, so by the central limit theorem x̄ is approximately normal.

items.answer: Type I and Type II errors are not complementary: a Type II error is not rejecting H₀ when it is false, and its probability depends on the true value of p, which is not given.

items.stem: The number of meteors seen by an observer in Toronto in a 10-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.5. The test uses the number, X, in a randomly chosen 20-minute period; H₀ is rejected if X ≤ 1. Find the probability of a Type I error.

In the past, 30% of the customers at a café in Istanbul ordered a cold drink. After the menu is changed, the owner wishes to test whether this proportion has increased. The test is based on 25 customers and uses a 10% significance level. (a) State suitable hypotheses and find the critical region. (b) Find the probability of a Type I error.
The critical region of a test is
options: the set of values for which H₀ is accepted as true
the value of the test statistic observed
the set of values of the test statistic for which H₀ is rejected
the region where H₁ is proved
items.answer: the set of values of the test statistic for which H₀ is rejected

items.stem: In the past, 20% of the customers at a café in Lisbon ordered a cold drink. After the menu is changed, the owner wishes to test whether this proportion has increased. In a random sample of 10 customers after the change, 4 ordered a cold drink. A test is carried out at the 10% significance level. Mei calculates P(X = 4) = 0.0881 and compares this with 0.1. Explain the mistake.
items.answer: The test must use the probability of a result at least as extreme as 4: P(X ≥ 4) = 0.121, which is then compared with 0.1.
items.markingKey: B1 tail probability needed, not P(X = 4); B1 P(X ≥ 4) = 0.121 [2]

items.stem: In the past, 30% of the buses on a route in Karachi arrived late. After a new timetable is introduced, the bus company tests whether the proportion of late buses has increased. Of 18 randomly chosen buses after the change, 8 arrived late. State suitable hypotheses for a test at the 2.5% significance level and, given that P(X ≥ 8) = 0.141, state the conclusion.
items.answer: H₀: p = 0.3, H₁: p > 0.3. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the proportion of late buses has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 0.3, H₁: p > 0.3; M1 compare with 0.025; A1 conclusion in context [3]

items.stem: A standard treatment for a condition is successful for 40% of patients. Doctors in Cairo test whether a new treatment is more successful. Of 24 randomly chosen patients given the new treatment, the number treated successfully is 11. (a) Explain why a one-tailed test is appropriate. (b) Explain what is meant by the significance level in this context. (c) State one assumption needed for the binomial model to be valid.
items.answer: (a) The suspicion is only that the new treatment is more successful, in one direction. (b) The probability, 0.01, of concluding that the new treatment is more successful when in fact p = 0.4. (c) The patients are independent of each other (with the same probability of success for each).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 [1] (b) B1 probability of rejecting H₀ when true; B1 in context [2] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: A test consists of multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A teacher wishes to test whether Lucas does better than guessing at random. The number of customers arriving at a shop in Nairobi in a 5-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 3. After an advertising campaign, the owner wishes to test whether the mean number of customers arriving has increased. In a randomly chosen 10-minute period, the number of customers arriving is 12. The test is at the 1% significance level. Freya uses X ~ Po(3) and finds P(X ≥ 12) = 7.14 × 10⁻⁵. Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The mean must be scaled to a 10-minute period: X ~ Po(6), giving P(X ≥ 12) = 0.0201. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean number of customers arriving has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 mean should be 6; M1 0.0201; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The number of flaws in a 1-metre length of fabric from a mill has a Poisson distribution with mean 0.6. After a new loom is installed, the manager wishes to test whether the mean number of flaws has increased. In a randomly chosen 4-metre length, the number of flaws is 8. The test is at the 2.5% significance level. Lucas uses X ~ Po(0.6) and finds P(X ≥ 8) = 2.45 × 10⁻⁷. Identify the error and give the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The mean must be scaled to a 4-metre length: X ~ Po(2.4), giving P(X ≥ 8) = 0.00334. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean number of flaws has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 mean should be 2.4; M1 0.00334; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: Lina suspects that an ordinary six-sided die shows a six more often than it should. The die is thrown 15 times and shows a six 5 times. Test at the 1% significance level whether the die shows a six more often than it should.
items.answer: H₀: p = 1/6, H₁: p > 1/6; P(X ≥ 5) = 0.0898 > 0.01. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the die shows a six more often than it should.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: p = 1/6, H₁: p > 1/6; M1 P(X ≥ 5) with X ~ B(15, 1/6) = 1 − P(X ≤ 4); A1 0.0898; M1 compare with 0.01; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The number of earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more in a region in a year has a Poisson distribution with mean 1.5. A geologist wishes to test whether the mean number of such earthquakes has increased. In a randomly chosen 5-year period, the number of such earthquakes is 16. Carry out the test at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: H₀: λ = 1.5, H₁: λ > 1.5; X ~ Po(7.5); P(X ≥ 16) = 0.00461 < 0.01. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean number of earthquakes has increased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: λ = 1.5, H₁: λ > 1.5 (or in terms of the mean for a 5-year period); B1 mean for a 5-year period = 7.5; M1 P(X ≥ 16) with X ~ Po(7.5) = 1 − P(X ≤ 15); A1 0.00461; M1 compare with 0.01; A1 conclusion in context [6]

items.stem: The number of customers arriving at a shop in Madrid in a 5-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 3. After an advertising campaign, the owner wishes to test whether the mean number of customers arriving has decreased. The test uses the number in a randomly chosen 20-minute period and a 1% significance level. (a) State the null and alternative hypotheses. (b) Find the critical region. (c) State the probability of a Type I error.

The times taken by employees in Nairobi to complete a task have mean 36 minutes and standard deviation 3 minutes. After a training session, the manager wishes to test whether the mean time has changed. 36 randomly chosen employees who attended the training have a mean time of 36.7 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Find the value of the test statistic z.

The reaction times of drivers in a simulator test have mean 250 ms and standard deviation 40 ms. A researcher wishes to test whether the mean reaction time of drivers who have just used a phone is lower. A random sample of 100 drivers who have just used a phone has mean reaction time 246 ms. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. The test is at the 2.5% significance level. Amara calculates z = (246 − 250)/(40²/100) = −0.250. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The variance σ²/n has been used instead of the standard deviation σ/√n; z = −1.000. Do not reject H₀. There is insufficient evidence at the 2.5% significance level that the mean reaction time of such drivers is lower.
items.markingKey: B1 square root of σ²/n needed; M1 z = −1.000; A1 conclusion [3]

items.stem: The journey times on a bus route in Muscat have mean 50 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. After a new bus lane opens, the bus company wishes to test whether the mean journey time has decreased. 36 randomly chosen journeys after the bus lane opens have a mean time of 47.2 minutes. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean journey time has decreased.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 50, H₁: μ < 50; z = −2.800 < −1.645. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 5% significance level that the mean journey time has decreased.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 50, H₁: μ < 50; M1 z = (47.2 − 50)/(6/√36); A1 −2.800; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine are normally distributed with mean 500 ml and standard deviation 8 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is more than this. A random sample of 20 cartons has mean volume 505 ml. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean volume is more than this.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ > 500; z = 2.795 > 2.326. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean volume is more than this.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ > 500; M1 z = (505 − 500)/(8/√20); A1 2.795; M1 compare with 2.326; A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: The volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine have mean 330 ml and standard deviation 4 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is different from this. A random sample of 80 cartons has mean volume 331.6 ml. Assume that the standard deviation is unchanged. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean volume is different from this.
items.answer: H₀: μ = 330, H₁: μ ≠ 330; z = 3.578 > 2.576. Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 1% significance level that the mean volume is different from this.
items.markingKey: B1 H₀: μ = 330, H₁: μ ≠ 330; M1 z = (331.6 − 330)/(4/√80); A1 3.578; M1 compare with 2.576 (two-tailed); A1 conclusion in context [5]

items.stem: In the past, the volumes of juice in cartons filled by a machine had mean 1000 ml. An inspector wishes to test whether the mean volume is more than this. For a random sample of 50 cartons, the values x ml satisfy Σx = 50040 and Σx² = 50080377.4. (a) Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean volume is more than this. (b) State, with a reason, whether the conclusion would be the same at the 1% significance level.
items.answer: (a) H₀: μ = 1000, H₁: μ > 1000; z = 2.131; Reject H₀. There is sufficient evidence at the 10% significance level that the mean volume is more than this. (b) Critical value 2.326; z = 2.131, so do not reject H₀; a different conclusion.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 H₀: μ = 1000, H₁: μ > 1000; M1 z = (1000.8 − 1000)/√(7.049/50); A1 2.131; M1 compare with 1.282; A1 conclusion in context [5] (b) M1 compare with 2.326; A1 correct comparison [2]

items.stem: Yusuf suspects that a coin is biased against heads. The test uses 18 tosses at the 1% significance level, and H₀ is rejected if X ≤ 3. Diego says: "P(Type I error) = 0.00377, so P(Type II error) = 1 − 0.00377 = 0.996." Explain why Diego is wrong.
items.answer: Type I and Type II errors are not complementary: a Type II error is not rejecting H₀ when it is false, and its probability depends on the true value of p, which is not given.
items.markingKey: B1 not complementary; B1 depends on the true value of p [2]

items.stem: A standard treatment for a condition is successful for 30% of patients. Doctors in Bangkok test whether a new treatment is more successful. The test uses 25 patients at the 10% significance level, and H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 11. Yusuf says: "P(Type I error) = 0.0978, so P(Type II error) = 1 − 0.0978 = 0.902." Explain why Yusuf is wrong.
items.answer: Type I and Type II errors are not complementary: a Type II error is not rejecting H₀ when it is false, and its probability depends on the true value of p, which is not given.
items.markingKey: B1 not complementary; B1 depends on the true value of p [2]

items.stem: The number of customers arriving at a shop in Cairo in a 5-minute period has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.5. After an advertising campaign, the owner wishes to test whether the mean number of customers arriving has increased. The test uses the number, X, in a randomly chosen 20-minute period; H₀ is rejected if X ≥ 15. Find the probability of a Type I error.

Omar suspects that a coin is biased against heads. The test is based on 18 tosses and uses a 5% significance level. (a) State suitable hypotheses and find the critical region. (b) Explain, in context, what is meant by a Type II error.
items.answer: (a) H₀: p = 0.5, H₁: p < 0.5; X ≤ 5 (b) Concluding that there is no evidence that the coin is biased against heads when in fact it is.
